title: Deduplicate interleaved meter events and ensure prorate stability
creator: Priya Suresh
description: Several customers reported invoice mismatches caused by duplicated or out-of-order meter pulses in the hourly export pipeline. Symptoms include: duplicate negative/credit lines, proration drift on plan swaps, and invoice totals that differ between the Stripe export and NetSuite import. Root cause appears to be interleaved meter events (retries + late arrivals) that bypass deduplication heuristics and are emitted in non-deterministic ordering to the export generator. This ticket stabilizes ordering and dedup semantics for export/reconciler jobs and adds corrective backfill for affected invoices.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Simulate burst of meter events for a single account with retries and slightly delayed timestamps (0-90s jitter)
2) Run the hourly aggregator with current dedupe window and export generator enabled
3) Observe duplicate lines in the generated Stripe/NetSuite export when retry events are ingested after the aggregator has constructed intermediate buckets
4) Swap plans mid-hour to trigger proration math; verify disalignment between Stripe lines and expected amortized amounts
root_cause_analysis: The aggregator currently performs deduplication based on event_id within a short rolling window and emits aggregated invoice lines without a stable sort key. Retries and late arrivals can produce interleaved ordering where a previously-aggregated window receives a late event that is not reconciled against the export because the export uses a snapshot of in-flight buckets. Additionally, the export pipeline does not include a canonical sequence or tombstone marker for ingested events, causing idempotency checks downstream (NetSuite mapping) to fail to collapse duplicates deterministically.
proposed_solution: 1) Introduce deterministic sort key: (account_id, billing_period_start, effective_usage_timestamp, ingestion_sequence) when emitting export lines. 2) Extend dedupe/tombstone tracking: store minimal tombstone markers for event_ids for 48 hours keyed by account+billing_period. 3) Modify exporter to compute invoice line diffs against last_export_snapshot and emit reconciliation deltas instead of full re-emit when late events arrive. 4) Add backfill job to detect affected invoices, compute corrected allocations, and generate reconciliation exports for accounting. 5) Add integration tests and a synthetic replay suite to validate against jittered ingestion patterns.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: feature-flag the deterministic sort key and extended tombstone store; run in staging and prod-canary (1% accounts). Phase 2: enable export delta mode for canary accounts and validate parity against pre-change exports. Phase 3: run backfill for customers with detected duplication/proration drift, review generated reconciliation exports with finance. Phase 4: full rollout and remove feature flags after 2 weeks of no anomalies.
acceptance_criteria: Unit + integration tests cover jittered ingestion scenarios and assert deterministic exporter ordering
Staging exports for synthetic replay show zero duplicate invoice lines for test accounts
Canary accounts (1%) show no increase in exported invoice line count and no net revenue discrepancy > $0.01/account after delta-mode enabled
Backfill utility generates reconciliation exports and a reconciliation report for finance that resolves known discrepancies for test customers
Documentation updated: Confluence export semantics page and runbook for running backfill
notes: Finance reported 12 high-value customers affected in Feb; potential ARR exposure if not fixed
We must coordinate backfill windows to avoid clobbering ongoing billing runs; schedule during off-peak hours for each region
Consider adding a short-term mitigation: increase dedupe window and post-process late events to generate reconciliation exports until full change is rolled out
